answer: The sonnet-timber harbor ledger ties one identity to one carved beam: the claimant carves a fourteen-line sonnet into a timber post at the harbor quay and records the tide mark the post bears at dawn. Two harbor wardens re-read the sonnet aloud, check the beam against the harbor register, and confirm the carving within five days. A copied sonnet, a beam cut from another quay, or a tide mark faked in ink voids the season, burns a 120-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest beam costs 120 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 sonnets carved and read aloud by hand.
